title: NFO metadata writer for multi-episode files might be broken
body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing open and closed issues

### Current Behavior

There difference seems to be that the 4.0.15 NFO (which works with Jellyfin) does not contain lines containing `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" standalone="yes"?>`.

I don't know if this is a problem with Jellyfin or Sonarr. I know neither about nfo nor xml specs. I tried putting both versions in XML validators and both fail with different results.

### Expected Behavior

Jellyfin should be able to recognise from the NFO file that the single video file contains multiple episodes.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Import a series in Sonarr in which each video file contains multiple episodes. (In my case these are externally downloaded.)
2. Go to "Manage Episodes"
3. Assign episodes to the corresponding files.
4. Click "Import"
5. Click "Refresh & Scan"
6. Refresh metadata in Jellyfin

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)
- Sonarr: 4.0.16.2944
- Docker Install: Yes (Podman)
- Using Reverse Proxy: No
- Browser: Not relevant
- Database: Sqlite
```

### What branch are you running?

Main

### Trace Logs?

Not needed I think.

### Anything else?

_No response_
author: kartikynwa

comments.author: thezoggy
comments.body:
per docs on jellyfin and support form, the line to define the xml deceleration is present in every example and note. so i doubt this is your actual issue and more of the fact of where the .nfo is placed/named or just stale caching on your side.

which metadata option are you using? I assume its xbmc as that was the one that recently got updated...  why not use plex?

settings > metadata > ??

comments.author: kartikynwa
comments.body:
@thezoggy I am using the Emby exporter. Felt the natural choice since Jellyfin is an Emby fork and it has worked well for years. And still does except for this small issue. > more of the fact of where the .nfo is placed/named or just stale caching on your side No. The NFO is placed where it should be and I am rebuilding Jellyfin metadata from scratch to make sure. > the line to define the xml deceleration is present in every example and note This is true. After reading this I did some more testing. If there is only declaration line (at the top of the file), the metadata is read as it should.
Screenshot
The problem seems to be that there are three declarations in the 4.0.16 NFO. If I use that NFO then the metadata is not read properly.
Screenshot
If I remove the second and third declarations the metadata is parsed properly again.

comments.author: thezoggy
comments.body: Indeed the multiple declarations is not expected, only noticed the top entry and thought that was what you were calling out as the issue.  Ty for reporting
